current: Protein made in Vietnam for people, from domestic inputs where possible, adds a second source.
proposed: Make the condition explicit: only routes on domestic protein or carbon inputs (fermentation on cassava or sugar with domestic urea; rice, peanut, seaweed protein) reduce import dependence; routes on imported soy, pea, gluten or mung bean move it, often to China (about 84% of imported food plant-protein tonnage, 2025) or Myanmar. Add: at D-BENCH 2035 the net saving of imported soy protein is at most about 0.2% of soybean-meal protein fed (our calculation).

current: Feed-price shocks 2022 and 2026; ASF in 2019 and 2025
proposed: Add the consumer side: pork prices up 57.23% in 2020 (1.94 points of a 3.23% CPI rise) after ASF; in 2022 foods up only 1.62% and pork down 10.68% while feed costs rose. Imported-feed shocks land mainly on farm margins; disease shocks reach consumers. Note that 2026 is not yet clear: food and food services rose 4.76% in January to August 2026, with no item breakdown that separates feed, energy and the 2025 ASF wave.

current: Feed-price shocks in 2022 and 2026 and African swine fever show the exposure.
proposed: Say whom each exposure protects: imported feed is mainly a producer, processor and trade-balance exposure; the consumer price exposure is mainly disease (line L2).

where: ch01-why-vietnam section 1.1 (only if L4 does not add it)
current: Rice still supplies 27.0 g of protein a day and soy foods only 4.9 g
proposed: Add: soy foods (4.94 g) and wheat (3.27 g) are almost entirely imported, so about 8% of protein supply (about 305 kt of protein a year) is imported plant protein eaten directly; tofu and soy milk are part of the Americas soy dependence.

current: Protein-security indicator: the share of the protein people eat that is made from domestic inputs
proposed: Anchor it: Resolution 34/NQ-CP (food security to 2030) has no import, feed or protein indicator; MAE's 2026 plan task to reduce import dependence by developing domestic raw-material areas is the official hook. Define the indicator by input origin, not place of processing.

Add Resolution 34/NQ-CP (25 Mar 2021) rows: rice land 3.5 million ha; paddy at least 35 Mt; vegetables and beans 23 to 24 Mt; carcass meat 6.0 to 6.5 Mt; fresh milk 2.6 Mt; eggs 23 billion; aquatic 9 to 10 Mt; energy above 2,500 kcal per person per day; stunting below 19%; diets with less rice and more meat, milk, eggs and fish. Status: aquatic met (9.95 Mt in 2025); milk about 50% (1.3 Mt in 2025; 1.37 Mt planned for 2026).
Add: the national food-security resolution has no import, feed, soybean, protein or alternative-protein indicator; its 'diversify' refers to food products and nutrition.
Add a window: successor to Resolution 34/NQ-CP, MAE, by 2030 (our inference; none announced); could carry a protein import-dependence indicator.

current: PSB-001 to PSB-023; China row is the soybean-meal reduction plan
proposed: Add PSB-024: China, State Council General Office opinions on the big food view (Guobanfa [2024] No. 46, 12 Sep 2024): calories and protein from plants, animals and microbes; microbial cell protein promoted for feed; new foods steadily and cautiously; non-grain biomass sugar; system formed by 2027 and built by 2035; no volume target; a big-food statistics system. Note that the 2026 No. 1 document keeps biomanufacturing, does not repeat 'new food resources' and adds import diversification.

where: ch20-drivers-2050 section 20.2 (Political framing row); ch24-vision-2050 framing paragraph
current: Security framing in EU, Japan, Korea; Singapore dropped 30 by 30
proposed: Add China: security framing with microbial protein mainly for feed and on domestic non-grain carbon (2024); 'new food resources' not repeated in the 2026 No. 1 document. Peers do not count alternative protein made from imported inputs as security.

where: ch20-drivers-2050 section 20.1 (Shrinking capture fisheries row); app-f2-drivers-signals F2.5.6
current: Capture to fall from about 3.8 Mt (2025) to 2.8 Mt (2030) (official target)
proposed: Add: marine standing stock about 3.95 Mt (2016 to 2020), 22.1% below 2000 to 2005, while capture rose; climate change cuts catch potential in Viet Nam's EEZ by 2.8 to 6.8% (RCP2.6) and 4.3 to 11.7% (RCP8.5) by 2050 in two FAO models. Fishing pressure and policy outweigh climate to 2050.

current: Dated SSP projections for shrimp, pangasius and anchoveta: open
proposed: Partly closed for wild capture in Viet Nam's waters (RCP-based, FAO 627); still open for shrimp, pangasius and anchoveta (OQ-138 stays open).

current: 17 shocks; SHK-010 (2022) gives import prices only
proposed: Add SHK-018 consumer pork price shock 2020 (+57.23%; 1.94 CPI points) and SHK-019 2008 food price spike (CPI +22.97%; staples over 49%; other foods over 32%). Extend SHK-010 notes: 2022 consumer foods +1.62%, pork minus 10.68%. Lesson: disease reaches consumers; input shocks reach farmers. Add to SHK-013 (2026) notes: consumer food and food services +4.76% (January to August 2026 average), no item breakdown.

Add: the 2024 Red Sea crisis raised Vietnamese container export rates (US East Coast USD 2,600 to 4,100 to 4,500, December 2023 to January 2024); we found no evidence it affected soy, maize or food-protein imports.

current: Axis 1: feed-protein import stress; axis 2: Asia's fermentation market
proposed: Keep the axes. Add a reading: in the Chinese-dominance worlds (SC-B, SC-D), food alternative protein made from Chinese ingredients raises dependence on China; only domestic-input routes add security in SC-C and SC-D.
